result:
**I'd eliminate tribalism.**

Not in some utopian "everyone holds hands" way—that's naive. I mean the deep, instinctive wiring that makes humans sort ourselves into "us vs. them" over *everything*: politics, religion, nationality, ideology, even which streaming service you use. It's the root poison. It turns reasonable disagreements into holy wars, lets obvious lies flourish because they're *our* lies, and keeps us from solving actual problems because admitting the other side might have a point feels like betrayal.

If that single psychological bug was patched out of humanity tomorrow—replaced with a default setting of "curious skepticism and intellectual honesty"—most of our worst problems would start dissolving. We'd still argue. We'd still have competing interests. But we wouldn't *need* to demonize each other to feel secure. Science, philosophy, and genuine progress would accelerate because good ideas could win on merit instead of tribal affiliation.

Everything else (AI alignment, space colonization, fixing energy, curing diseases) becomes dramatically easier when the species stops shooting itself in the foot every five minutes out of spite or signaling.

One change. Maximum leverage.
